posts.text: ⛽ The UK will freeze fuel duty again in Wednesday's Budget and keep the 5p discount, the BBC reports. Tariffs on 100 food items will also go, saving households up to £21 a year. Gilts and the pound will watch the fiscal cost. #UKBudget #GBP

🤖 Nvidia will invest $3 billion in Meta, which plans to raise $95 billion for AI infrastructure through share sales. Meta will expand use of Nvidia's Vera Rubin chips. Both stocks were flat premarket; AI capex remains a key driver for tech. #Nvidia #AI

🇺🇦 Russia hit Ukraine overnight with ballistic missiles and 280 drones, mainly targeting Kyiv; air defences stopped two missiles and 255 drones. In Kyiv one woman was killed and 15 people were injured. Risk sentiment stays fragile. #Ukraine #Markets

🏦 HSBC said profit jumped 32% and it will hand $2.7bn (£2bn) to shareholders, helped by cost cuts and lower legal bills. Its shares still fell over 6% in London, a day before the UK Budget amid calls for higher bank taxes. #HSBC #FTSE

📈 South Korea's economy grew 1.0% in Q3 from the prior quarter and 3.4% year on year, well above the Bank of Korea's 0.3% forecast, as AI chip exports rose. Private consumption fell 0.2%. Chip demand remains a key support for Asian markets. #SouthKorea #AI

🗳️ Israelis vote today in an election seen as a referendum on Netanyahu. Most polls show his coalition losing its Knesset majority, with the opposition also short of 61 seats, pointing to long coalition talks. Regional risk stays in focus. #Israel #Markets

🏦 HSBC's third-quarter pretax profit rose 32% to $9.6 billion, largely in line with estimates, as revenue climbed to $18.6 billion. The bank announced a share buyback of up to $1 billion; its shares fell 2.95% in Hong Kong. #HSBC #Earnings

🛒 The FTC and 20 states sued Dollar General on Monday, alleging it charged shoppers more than shelf, tag and ad prices after "tens of thousands" of complaints. Shares fell about 4%. Discount retailers face added scrutiny ahead of the midterms. #Retail #Stocks

🏦 The Fed is expected to hold rates at 3.75%-4% this week after last month's first hike since 2023. Futures price under a 10% chance of another hike now, but nearly 75% see one by year-end, with CPI at 3.7%. Rate-sensitive assets stay on edge. #Fed #Inflation

🛢️ Oil eased Monday as Saudi Arabia's defense minister met Iran's president in Tehran to ease tensions. Brent fell 20 cents to $116.52 a barrel and WTI 79 cents to $102.48, still up about 12% this month. Gulf supply risk stays in focus. #Oil

💼 Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 staff in the US, Canada, India and the UK, roughly 27% of its 223,000 workforce, a source told CNBC, as AI data center costs climb. Earnings are due Wednesday. #Microsoft #Stocks

🚀 Anthropic made its IPO filing public, planning a Nasdaq listing under the ticker "ANT" and showing an $80.7 billion loss in the first half of 2026. Wall Street opened higher as AI stays in focus, though doubts over AI spending linger. #Anthropic #IPO

🇬🇧 UK Chancellor John Healey will shield low-income pensioners from income tax in Wednesday's Budget with a new allowance. The state pension is set to rise 3.9% to £13,036.40 from April, above the £12,570 allowance. Gilts stay focused on fiscal math. #UKBudget
